issue_insights.summary_brief: 本次信号覆盖 19 个仓库，发现 5 组跨仓库共性问题，其中 WSL 认证未回退到凭证文件（影响 33 仓）和 monorepo 内 worktree 导致 pnpm workspace 污染（影响 176 仓）为最高优先级；单仓层面 workflow_runtime 类问题最为集中，多个 SDK 在流式响应聚合、API 契约处理上存在系统性缺陷。
global_highlights: **认证回退缺失**：WSL 环境下 Secret Service 不可用时未回退读取 ~/.credentials.json，导致跨 33 个仓库的 Linux/WSL 认证流程完全阻断
**Monorepo 污染风险**：worktree 创建在 monorepo 内部导致 pnpm/yarn workspace node_modules 被污染，影响 176 个仓库的主流程隔离机制
**SDK 流式聚合缺陷**：多个 SDK（Python/TypeScript/agno）在处理流式响应时丢失 structuredContent、_meta、container 等字段，导致 MCP Apps UI 渲染和代码执行续接失败
**Session 恢复后状态丢失**：LLM 成本追踪、plan 文件、非 transcript 状态在 session resume 后未能正确恢复，造成计费盲点和上下文断层

signals.topic: MCP tool wrapper silently drops structuredContent and _meta fields, breaking MCP Apps generative UI and observability
signals.summary: agno.tools.mcp.MCPTools drops both CallToolResult.structuredContent and CallToolResult._meta (the MCP spec's out-of-band metadata channel) when constructing the internal ToolResult. This has two concrete user impacts: (1) MCP Apps / AG-UI clients cannot render UI because the Prefab component tree in structuredContent is lost, forcing wasteful re-fetches; (2) any MCP server using _meta for trace ids, provenance, or rate-limit hints is unreachable through Agno. Both are silent drops — no error, just missing data. Issues #7686 and #7658 share the exact same root cause (libs/agno/agno/utils/mcp.py call_tool wrapper) and can be merged.
signals.review_reason: Two bugs with identical root cause in the same code path (libs/agno/agno/utils/mcp.py). structuredContent loss directly breaks MCP Apps generative UI rendering (AG-UI / CopilotKit integration). _meta loss breaks observability and structured metadata access. Both are silent failures — data is simply absent rather than errored, making them particularly insidious. Users must work around by re-fetching results, which is wasteful and non-obvious.

signals.topic: Streaming silently degrades to blocking when output_schema with parse_response=True is used, causing 504 gateway timeouts
signals.summary: When an Agent uses an output_schema (Pydantic model) with parse_response=True, calling agent.run(..., stream=True) or agent.print_response(..., stream=True) blocks until the entire LLM response is complete instead of streaming chunks. For long-running tasks, this causes network gateways (Nginx, Cloudflare, Load Balancers) to kill the connection with 504 Gateway Timeouts because no data flows over the wire during generation.
signals.review_reason: Direct user impact: stream=True is explicitly requested but silently ignored, causing 504 timeouts for long-running tasks. This is not a degraded experience — it is a complete functional failure of the streaming contract. The 504 timeout is a measurable production impact. Though count=1, the severity (complete functional failure of a documented feature + explicit user workaround failure) justifies P1.

source_issues.title: [Bug] Streaming degrades to non-streaming when using output_schema with parse_response=True

signals.topic: AccuracyResult raises AttributeError instead of returning None when all evaluator iterations fail, masking root cause
signals.summary: AccuracyResult.avg_score and sibling fields (mean_score, min_score, max_score, std_dev_score) are declared as field(init=False) but only assigned inside compute_stats() under a guard checking results length. When all evaluator iterations fail (provider errors, rate-limits, judge model failures), these fields are never assigned, and any access raises AttributeError. This masks the actual root cause with a confusing secondary error, including from the library's own AccuracyResult.print_summary.
aliases: avg_score AttributeError when no iterations succeed
signals.review_reason: Confusing secondary error that masks the actual failure, making debugging harder. The AttributeError surfaces in library-internal code (print_summary), meaning even default usage hits it. While only affecting evaluation workflows where all iterations fail (edge case), the error message is actively misleading and blocks the user's ability to understand what went wrong.

source_issues.title: [Bug] AccuracyResult.avg_score raises AttributeError when no iterations succeed
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: 'AccuracyResult' object has no attribute 'avg_score' raised from AccuracyResult.print_summary (library-internal) and any user code reading result.avg_score without guarding on result.results being non-empty. Masks the actual evaluator failure root cause.

signals.topic: TeamRunCompletedEvent arrives with session_state=None over SSE/streaming, breaking state-dependent downstream consumers
signals.summary: When a Team emits TeamRunCompletedEvent over a streaming run, the event consistently arrives with session_state=None even when tools have mutated run_context.session_state during the run. Downstream consumers (AG-UI, CopilotKit, custom integrations) that expect session_state to reflect post-run state are left with None and must make a separate GET /sessions/{id} call after the stream closes. Agent-side RunCompletedEvent populates session_state correctly — the team path was never updated to match.
signals.review_reason: session_state=None over streaming breaks downstream consumers that depend on post-run state (AG-UI, CopilotKit, custom integrations). Users must add a workaround GET call after every streaming team run. The inconsistency with agent-side behavior (which correctly populates session_state) makes this a clear regression from the intended contract established in PR #4975.

source_issues.title: [Bug] TeamRunCompletedEvent omits session_state over SSE / streaming
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed on agno 2.5.17 and 2.6.0. session_state=None even when tools have mutated it during the run. Agent-side RunCompletedEvent populates session_state correctly, but team equivalent never does. Downstream consumers must fall back to separate GET /sessions/{id} call after stream closes.

signals.topic: WhatsApp button reply messages trigger 'WARNING: Unknown message type: button', blocking user interaction with interactive templates

signals.review_reason: WhatsApp button interactions are a standard messaging pattern and users cannot complete a button-click flow — the agent simply never receives the user's input. This is a functional gap in WhatsApp integration, not merely a cosmetic warning. The user had to build a manual workaround using httpx middleware, which is not an acceptable solution for production WhatsApp bots.

signals.topic: invopop/jsonschema v0.14.0 incompatibility breaks SDK compilation in consuming modules

signals.review_reason: Build failure is a genuine user pain point: SDK consumers cannot compile their projects without a version-pinning workaround. This blocks the entire development workflow. Although count=1, the severity (complete build block) and explicit workaround requirement justify P1.

signals.topic: Embedded reflect.Type in SDK disables Go linker dead-code elimination for consuming projects

signals.review_reason: While real (binary bloat and DCE disabled is a known Go issue), this is a secondary packaging concern rather than a main-flow blocker. No compile failure or runtime crash reported — users can still ship binaries, just larger ones. Cross-referenced from another SDK's similar issue, giving it credibility, but impact is less acute than PP001/PP002. P2 is appropriate.

SyntaxError unhandled rejection crashing Node process

signals.topic: SDK strips directory paths from filenames in multipart uploads, breaking skills.versions.create()
signals.summary: The SDK's multipart form handler strips directory paths from File names by default (split(/[\\/]/).pop()), turning 'my-skill/SKILL.md' into 'SKILL.md'. The skills.versions.create() API strictly requires the top-level directory prefix in the filename, causing a 400 invalid_request_error on every skills version update.
aliases: multipart file path stripping breaks skills versioning API
skills.versions.create() 400 error due to path stripping
signals.review_reason: This blocks a key API endpoint (skills.versions.create()) from working, forcing users to delete and recreate entire skills instead of updating versions. The root cause (stripFilenames=true default in multipartFormRequestOptions) is clearly identified in the SDK code. P1 (not P0) because count=1 and single-repository scope.

source_issues.title: SDK strips directory paths from filenames in multipart uploads, breaking skills.versions.create()

signals.topic: TaskNotificationMessage fires prematurely while subagent is still running, causing cascade workflow failures
signals.summary: When orchestrators dispatch parallel subagents via Task tool, the SDK sometimes delivers TaskNotificationMessage (injected as <task-notification> SystemMessage) while the referenced subagent is still actively executing — with 76–850s of tool calls remaining. The orchestrator's event-driven pattern acts on the premature completion signal, dispatching downstream agents against non-existent files, re-dispatching stale researchers, and flooding the orchestrator with stale notifications. Non-deterministic: identical runs produce different behavior.
signals.review_reason: This is a clear main-flow failure: the core orchestrator + parallel subagent pattern is broken. The premature notification causes the orchestrator to act on false completion signals, leading to cascading downstream failures (wrong reviewer dispatches, wasted researcher re-runs, stale notification floods). User impact is significant: wasted compute time and cost. Despite count=1, this is non-deterministic and architecture-level, meaning it likely affects any production orchestrator user — P1 not P0 only because single-source report and non-deterministic nature reduce reproducibility confidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug] TaskNotificationMessage fires while subagent is still running (premature, not cross-turn leak)
source_issues.evidence: Orchestrator receives premature <task-notification> for all 5 parallel subagents while each is still mid-execution (R2 had 26/39 tools remaining, 466s before next tool). Cascade: reviewer subagents dispatched against missing files, 8 min wasted re-dispatching researchers, total run cost $21.51 vs baseline $22.33. Timeline screenshot shows notification at 16:35:16 while R2 subagent continues until 16:43:02. Non-deterministic: 1/2 identical runs triggered the issue.

signals.topic: Multi-pod HITL: no SDK recovery mechanism when pod crashes during can_use_tool wait
signals.summary: Production multi-pod Kubernetes deployments using HITL approval via can_use_tool have no way to recover a pending approval gate after pod restart. The SDK provides no awareness of interrupted HITL gates, no durable HITL state in SessionStore, and no way to stop/pause the CLI subprocess during the wait. Application must re-implement all coordination logic externally. Additionally, SessionStore's materialize_resume_session() does not restore non-transcript state (plan files, pending HITL decisions), so resumed sessions lose critical context.
aliases: can_use_tool state not durable across pods
signals.review_reason: Production-critical blocker for multi-pod deployments using HITL: pod crash during approval wait is an expected failure mode in Kubernetes, and the SDK provides zero recovery path. This forces every application to reinvent complex coordination logic (persisting pending decisions, detecting already-made decisions, re-injecting them on resume). The impact is a complete session failure — users must start over or implement their own state machine on top of the SDK, which defeats the purpose of using the SDK's built-in can_use_tool mechanism.

source_issues.title: Multi-pod HITL: no recovery mechanism when pod crashes during `can_use_tool` wait
source_issues.evidence: No SDK mechanism to recover pending can_use_tool gate on a different pod after original pod dies. SDK has no awareness of interrupted HITL gates. Application must externally persist pending decisions and detect already-made decisions on resumed session. CLI subprocess stays alive consuming memory/CPU/connection during multi-tenant wait — does not scale. materialize_resume_session() only restores transcripts and auth, not non-transcript state (plan files, pending HITL decisions).

signals.topic: bwrap sandbox does not mount /etc/hosts, breaking localhost DNS resolution in containerized proxy environments
signals.summary: When the SDK runs inside Docker containers using bwrap sandboxing, /etc/hosts is not bind-mounted into the sandbox namespace. In AWS Bedrock AgentCore runtimes where outbound traffic routes through a localhost proxy, any Bash tool command that calls AWS services fails with DNS resolution errors (socket.gaierror, ProxyConnectionError, botocore failures). This breaks core AWS integration for all sandboxed Bash tool uses in container environments with proxy routing. Workaround is to disable sandbox entirely, sacrificing security isolation.
aliases: bwrap sandbox DNS failure in containers
localhost proxy DNS resolution fails in sandbox
signals.review_reason: Key functionality (AWS API calls via Bash tool) is completely broken in containerized environments when sandbox is enabled. This is a regression from CLI 2.1.81. The forced workaround (disabling sandbox) has a direct security cost: untrusted Bash commands run without isolation. For users in AWS Bedrock AgentCore container environments — a core deployment target — the sandbox is effectively unusable, which means critical AWS integrations fail silently.

source_issues.title: bwrap sandbox does not mount /etc/hosts — breaks localhost DNS resolution in containers
source_issues.evidence: All AWS boto3 calls fail with 'socket.gaierror: [Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution' and 'Failed to resolve localhost' proxy errors when bwrap sandbox is enabled in Docker container with localhost proxy routing. Regression from CLI 2.1.81 (no bwrap) to 2.1.92 (bwrap introduced). Only workaround is sandbox.enabled=false, losing security isolation. AWS IAM credential fetch via container metadata endpoint also blocked.

signals.topic: SessionStore materialize_resume_session() does not preserve plan files or non-transcript session state
signals.summary: When resuming a session via materialize_resume_session(), plan files (plans/*.md) and other CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR state beyond transcripts and auth files are not materialized. For sessions interrupted while in plan mode (EnterPlanMode), this means plan context is lost on resume. This compounds the multi-pod HITL recovery problem and affects any multi-pod deployment relying on SessionStore for state durability.
aliases: plan state not restored on resume
non-transcript state lost on session resume
signals.review_reason: Session state loss on resume is a real UX impact: users in multi-pod/multi-deploy scenarios relying on SessionStore for durability will lose plan mode context if interrupted. This is not blocking the core SDK from functioning, but it breaks a key workflow (plan mode + session resume) for distributed deployments. P2 because it only affects plan-mode users and the count is 1, but the issue is well-documented with a clear user scenario.

source_issues.title: Is plan state preserved when resuming via `SessionStore` + `materialize_resume_session()`?
source_issues.evidence: materialize_resume_session() writes transcripts, auth files, and subagent transcripts to temp dir but does not include plan files (plans/*.md). For sessions interrupted in EnterPlanMode, plan context is not restored on resume. Questioned whether transcript alone is sufficient to reconstruct plan state, or whether the .md file on disk is required.

signals.topic: MCP servers launched by SDK not cleaned up on exit, leaving orphaned processes
signals.summary: When ClaudeAgentOptions configures MCP servers (e.g., chrome-devtools via npx), any prompt that launches a browser leaves that browser process open after the SDK exits. The SDK does not clean up MCP server processes it spawns, and there is no mechanism to register cleanup handlers for MCP server lifecycle.
aliases: orphaned MCP server processes on SDK exit
signals.review_reason: Process resource leak is a real user impact: orphaned browser processes accumulate over repeated SDK invocations, consuming system resources (memory, file descriptors, CPU). While not a workflow blocker, this is a negative experience that accumulates over time and is especially problematic in long-running services or automated test environments. The bug label and multiple comments confirm it is an active user issue.

source_issues.title: The sdk should clean up mcp servers it launches on exit
source_issues.evidence: MCP servers configured via ClaudeAgentOptions (e.g., chrome-devtools via npx chrome-devtools-mcp@latest) are not terminated when the SDK exits. Any browser launched by the MCP server remains open as an orphaned process. Four comments on the issue confirm it is a known, ongoing problem.

signals.topic: Linux glibc systems pick wrong musl binary variant, blocking query() main flow
signals.summary: SDK auto-discovery or runtime variant selector prefers musl binary before glibc on Linux, causing query() to fail with ENOENT on glibc systems (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 12 arm64). Both #296 (Ubuntu glibc) and #306 (Debian arm64 glibc) share the same root cause: wrong libc detection or wrong iteration order. Spawn failure does not trigger fallback to the correct glibc binary.
aliases: musl preferred over glibc on linux
signals.review_reason: Two independent issues on two different Linux distributions (Ubuntu glibc x64, Debian glibc arm64) both show the SDK's runtime libc detection or variant ordering is wrong, causing query() to crash immediately on startup. This is a primary-flow block for all Linux SDK users on glibc systems with multiple platform packages installed (common with pnpm) or with non-standard libc detection.

source_issues.title: Linux: musl binary preferred over glibc in v0.2.116 CLI auto-discovery
source_issues.evidence: query() fails with 'Claude Code native binary not found' on Ubuntu 24.04 glibc when both musl and glibc variants are installed via pnpm; musl binary is iterated first and spawn ENOENT does not trigger fallback

source_issues.title: v0.2.119 picks linux-arm64-musl variant on Debian (glibc) arm64 even when only linux-arm64 is installed

signals.topic: beta.sessions.events.stream() stream starvation — 4 of 5 sessions fail before any event arrives
signals.summary: When firing multiple beta.sessions.events.stream() calls, 4 out of 5 streams consistently fail with TypeError: stream error: terminated before any events arrive. The issue persists even with serial (non-parallel) execution, ruling out concurrency ceiling. Standard Messages API works reliably with identical auth/model, isolating the bug to beta.sessions lifecycle.
signals.review_reason: beta.sessions events API is a core SDK session-based feature. The bug causes 4/5 sessions to fail before receiving any event — a near-total failure rate that makes the feature unusable in practice. Serial execution failing at the same rate rules out concurrency as the cause, indicating a deeper session initialization or event-subscription race condition. This directly blocks the primary beta.sessions workflow.

source_issues.title: beta.sessions stream starvation — 4 of 5 parallel (and serial) sessions fail with TypeError: stream error: terminated before any events

signals.topic: query() with outputFormat json_schema crashes with null dereference on effortLevel

The error occurs inside the SDK/Claude Code engine before any structured output is returned, surfacing as result.subtype: 'error_during_execution'. The crash is deterministic for the minimal repro case, returns a misleading error, and spans multiple SDK releases. While the main flow can technically continue by bypassing structured output, this blocks a core production use case and surfaces as an opaque internal error rather than a clear validation message.

signals.topic: Non-interactive unsupported slash commands emit valid session_id but no transcript, breaking session resume
signals.summary: Running Claude Code in non-interactive mode with an unsupported built-in slash command (e.g. /status) causes the CLI to emit a session_id in system/init and result messages, but no transcript JSONL file is created. When a client stores this session_id and later calls --resume, it fails with 'No conversation found with session ID'. SDK clients commonly treat system/init.session_id as the authoritative id to store for future resumes.
aliases: session resume fails unsupported slash command
signals.review_reason: Session resumption is a primary SDK workflow for multi-turn conversations. When the first message is an unsupported slash command, the SDK appears to succeed and provides a session_id, but that id is unusable for resumption. This causes silent data loss for clients that persist session_id from system/init — the next user message will fail immediately on resume. The discrepancy between the emitted session_id (which looks valid) and the non-resumable state makes this especially deceptive.

signals.topic: OTel telemetry emits Anthropic-native token attribute names instead of OTel GenAI convention, causing silent zero token counts in observability backends
signals.summary: With telemetry enabled, the SDK emits token counts as `input_tokens`/`output_tokens` where downstream OTel GenAI-convention-aware tools (Langsmith, Honeycomb gen_ai views, Datadog LLM observability) expect `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`/`gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`. This causes observability backends to show span structure but zero token counts, making per-LLM cost attribution from traces impossible. The gap is silent — no parser errors, just zeroes.
signals.review_reason: OTel-based observability is a critical integration requirement for production deployments. The attribute name mismatch causes a silent failure — spans appear in the observability backend but all token counts are zero. This makes per-LLM cost attribution from traces impossible, forcing SDK consumers to build a second parallel pipeline outside of OTel. The impact is concrete and recurring for every LLM call, not a one-off edge case.

source_issues.title: OTel telemetry: token counts emitted as input_tokens/output_tokens instead of OTel GenAI semantic convention gen_ai.usage.*
source_issues.evidence: Explicit Langsmith probe shows claude_code.llm_request spans with total_tokens=0, prompt_tokens=0, completion_tokens=0 despite underlying API returning input_tokens=10, output_tokens=53; SDK already partially adopts GenAI convention for gen_ai.system and gen_ai.request.model but stops short on usage attributes; downstream consumer has to maintain a parallel local PostToolUse capture pipeline to get cost data

signals.topic: GitHub Actions workflow completely fails on every run due to 'directory mismatch' internal error (Bun fd tracking regression)

signals.review_reason: This is a P0 blocking regression. The action fails on EVERY triggered run with exit 1 before any Claude Code tool is dispatched. The user's entire automation pipeline is non-functional and they had to disable the workflow trigger. Issue #1246 confirms the same error is a confirmed Bun runtime bug in fd tracking, proving this is not environment-specific.

signals.topic: Internal Agent SDK sub-calls ignore ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL override, silently routing to wrong model through OpenRouter proxy and causing unexpected billing charges
signals.summary: When using ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL to route through an LLM gateway (e.g. OpenRouter), internal Agent SDK sub-calls (task dispatch, planning step, sub-agents) ignore the ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL environment variable and send the literal claude-sonnet-4-6 model name to the proxy. The proxy routes to the actual Sonnet provider and bills the user's proxy key for calls the user explicitly opted out of.
aliases: model preset override bypassed by internal SDK calls
signals.review_reason: This is a verified silent billing regression with direct financial impact. Users following the officially documented OpenRouter proxy setup are silently charged for Sonnet calls they explicitly opted out of. The issue has smoking-gun evidence from OpenRouter's own API logs showing a billed request with the wrong model alongside the runner's correct env vars. The top-level review output looks correct to users, hiding the billing leak — making it insidious. Regression was introduced in v1.0.104 (claude-cli 2.1.118) and persists through v1.0.107. Downgraded from P0 because count=1 and it does not block the primary workflow (sub-call Sonnet charges are the harm, not workflow failure).

source_issues.title: Action ignores ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL for internal Agent SDK sub-calls (regression in v1.0.104 / claude-cli 2.1.118)

Regression confirmed to v1.0.104 / claude-cli 2.1.118 (first Sonnet-leak day after 7 clean days on v1.0.99-v1.0.103). Confirmed financial impact: USD ~$1.16 across two days on the affected repo. Root cause: sub-calls bypass env var override and send literal Sonnet name.

signals.topic: GitHub Actions cache save repeatedly fails on successive PR runs, burning 20-30 seconds per failure due to 5-retry exponential backoff on non-retryable key collision

The cache save repeatedly fails and wastes 20-30s per retry (5 retries = 2-5 minutes total) on every repeated PR run. While not workflow-blocking, the consistent wasted time across all repeated runs is a noticeable cost burden. Downgraded to P2 because count=1 and the workflow itself completes (just slower), unlike the directory mismatch regression which kills every run entirely.

signals.topic: Bundled GitHub MCP servers (github_comment, github_inline_comment) silently fail to spawn on pull_request events, breaking PR review automation

github_comment MCP tool not available despite config build

signals.topic: execution_file output not written when SDK throws on error_max_turns, causing data loss for downstream metrics consumers
signals.summary: When Claude Code reaches max-turns and the SDK throws an error, the execution_file (stored at $RUNNER_TEMP/claude-execution-output.json) is never written because the write happens after the try/catch block and the catch re-throws first. The result object prints to stdout but the structured file is absent. Any downstream step depending on steps.<id>.outputs.execution_file receives no data.
aliases: SDK throw prevents execution file write
signals.review_reason: This is a data loss bug with direct downstream impact. The messages array with all conversation turns is accumulated in memory before the throw, but is discarded when the catch block re-throws. Downstream steps relying on the execution_file output (for cost, turn count, duration, tool error metrics) get nothing. P2 because count=1 and the workflow does complete with stdout output — the harm is specifically lost structured data for consumers using the output artifact.

source_issues.title: execution_file output not written when SDK throws on error_max_turns
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in base-action/src/run-claude-sdk.ts: writeFile call is after the try/catch block, so when SDK throws (e.g. 'Reached maximum number of turns'), the catch re-throws before writeFile is reached. messages array is already populated with all turns before failure — data exists in memory and is lost. signals.topic: Telegram plugin: zombie bun server.ts processes accumulate indefinitely, causing unbounded CPU/memory consumption and blocking new sessions
signals.summary: Long-running Claude Code users accumulate orphaned bun server.ts processes from the Telegram plugin (6 zombies consuming 330-550% CPU; up to 73 concurrent pollers on same token). SIGTERM is never escalated to SIGKILL; stale-PID detection only tracks one PID; orphan watchdog uses .unref() and fails when the event loop is blocked. The Telegram plugin's process lifecycle management is fundamentally broken.
signals.review_reason: Three independent issues all describing the same root cause family: Telegram plugin process lifecycle management failures leading to unbounded zombie process accumulation. User impact is severe — critical resource consumption (330-550% CPU, up to 73 processes), sessions become increasingly resource-constrained, and only kill -9 works as workaround. All three issues have detailed root cause analysis with file/line references. Count=3 meets the high-frequency threshold for P0.

source_issues.title: [telegram] bun server.ts processes accumulate as zombies, consuming high CPU
source_issues.evidence: 6 zombie processes consuming 50-92% CPU each (330-550% combined), elapsed times 3-21 days. Only kill -9 works; SIGTERM ignored. Root cause: unhandledRejection/uncaughtException only log, stale detection tracks only one PID, no SIGKILL escalation, orphan watchdog .unref() fails when event loop blocked.

source_issues.title: telegram: orphan watchdog and stale-PID check both fail under wrapper-shell, allowing unbounded poller accumulation
source_issues.evidence: 73 live bun server.ts processes all polling the same bot token. Root cause: stale-PID check only knows one PID, orphan watchdog fails under wrapper shell chain (ppid check misses grandchild orphaned to init), 409 retry cap never triggers.

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin: stale server.ts can spin at 100% CPU — SIGTERM fallback missing
source_issues.evidence: Stale process enters 409-Conflict retry loop, signal handler never runs, SIGTERM ignored. Process spins at 100% CPU indefinitely. No SIGKILL fallback and no backoff on 409 errors.

signals.topic: Telegram and Discord plugins: typing indicator disappears before long Claude responses arrive, making bot appear unresponsive

aliases: bot appears unresponsive during long responses
signals.review_reason: Same defect manifests identically in two separate plugins (Telegram and Discord): typing indicator is a single fire-and-forget call, expiring well before long Claude responses complete. This is not a minor UX polish — when users send a message and see no typing feedback for 10+ seconds, they perceive the bot as broken or disconnected. Both reporters have working patches, confirming the fix is straightforward but the bug is real and recurring.

source_issues.title: telegram: typing indicator only visible for first ~5 seconds of long responses
source_issues.evidence: Telegram plugin sends sendChatAction('typing') exactly once on message arrival. Telegram clears after ~5s. Long Claude responses (>30s) cause bot to appear unresponsive. Reporter has working ~25-line patch.

source_issues.title: vercel/deployments-cicd skill: document PKCS#8 key requirement for GitHub Apps on Node.js 20 / OpenSSL 3

signals.topic: Non-OpenAI CUA clients (Google/Anthropic/Microsoft) drop captcha context notes, causing repeated captcha failures and task deadends

Non-OpenAI CUA providers silently dropping these notes causes the agent to make already-resolved captcha attempts repeatedly, which directly blocks task continuation — a primary workflow failure. This is not a minor parity gap; it is a functional regression for any user using Google, Anthropic, or Microsoft CUA providers in captcha-protected environments.

source_issues.title: core(cua): implement addContextNote parity for Google/Anthropic/Microsoft clients

This causes the agent to retry captcha interactions that have already been resolved, leading to task deadends. Related merged work #2023 and #1954 confirm this is an established feature.

signals.topic: Agent enters infinite web_search ↔ web_fetch tool loop, bypassing loop detection middleware and exhausting step budget without producing final output
signals.summary: The LoopDetectionMiddleware does not catch alternating tool patterns (web_search → web_fetch → web_search). The middleware uses hash-based detection of entire tool call sets and frequency-based single-tool thresholds, but alternating calls produce different hashes and neither tool individually hits frequency limits fast enough. Combined with context compaction causing the model to forget previously fetched results, the agent can make 200+ tool calls without reaching synthesis phase, consuming the entire step budget and producing no final report.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary workflow blocker. The agent's main task (web research) is fundamentally broken — it loops indefinitely through 200+ tool calls without ever producing a usable output. Users running any task requiring iterative web research will see their run exhaust the entire step budget and produce nothing. The issue is well-documented with root cause analysis and has 5 comments indicating active community engagement.

source_issues.title: Bug: Infinite web_search ↔ web_fetch tool-calling loop bypasses LoopDetectionMiddleware
source_issues.evidence: Agent enters a 200+ tool call loop alternating between web_search and web_fetch without being caught. Loop continues until recursion_limit (default 100) is hit, consuming entire step budget with no final report produced. Root cause: hash-based loop detection only matches identical tool call sets; frequency-based detection only tracks single-tool counts. Alternating pattern produces different hashes each response and neither tool individually hits 50-call threshold fast enough.

This directly meets the '主流程失败/阻断' and '明显成本损失' criteria.

signals.topic: Sandbox host-gateway connectivity causes false startup failures, with agent misjudging working sandbox as failed
signals.summary: DeerFlow's sandbox uses host-gateway address to connect to containers, but this frequently fails to connect even when the sandbox is actually running (verified by direct host IP + exposed port). LangGraph interprets this as sandbox startup failure and aborts the workflow, despite the sandbox being functional. Users have no reliable way to diagnose whether the failure is real or a false positive from the connectivity check.

signals.topic: Windows PowerShell 5.1: all bash tool execution broken due to unsupported && chaining, completely blocking host command execution

This causes all host commands to fail at shell parsing, completely blocking the agent's ability to run scripts, check ports, or execute any Windows host operations. The workaround of using cmd /c also fails due to security filter falsely flagging it as unsafe.
signals.review_reason: This completely blocks the agent from executing any host commands on Windows — a major platform. The issue states the agent 'completely loses the ability to execute host machine commands', making any workflow requiring Windows host interaction impossible. The bug is closed, suggesting it may be fixed, but its presence in this dataset confirms user impact.

signals.topic: make dev fails on macOS due to nginx error_log Permission denied at Homebrew compile-time path
signals.summary: Running make dev on macOS with Homebrew-installed nginx fails immediately because nginx attempts to open its compile-time default error_log path (/opt/homebrew/var/log/nginx/error.log, owned by root) before parsing the http {} block in nginx.local.conf. Since the error_log directive is only specified inside http {} (a lower-priority context), the permission-denied error occurs before it takes effect. Users cannot run make dev at all on macOS without manual intervention or root privileges.
signals.review_reason: This is a complete startup crash that prevents macOS developers from using the project at all. make dev fails immediately with no usable development environment. The error message is opaque (nginx internal behavior) requiring nginx internals knowledge to diagnose. The regression is identical to a previously-fixed issue (#870 for nginx.pid), confirming the pattern.

signals.topic: Proot-distro / Termux environment causes performance degradation (slow startup, high latency, lag)
signals.summary: Running Gemini CLI inside proot-distro (Termux on Android) causes slower startup, noticeable tool execution latency, streaming response lag, and higher CPU usage compared to native environments, making the CLI barely usable for the growing mobile developer audience using Termux.
signals.review_reason: Performance degradation in proot/Termux environments is a real and reproducible issue affecting mobile developers. The problem is detailed with root cause analysis (syscall overhead, FS access). However, count=1 and only a single-OS environment is affected, so P2 is appropriate. The suggested solution (proot detection + optimizations) is feasible and would broaden the CLI's audience.

source_issues.title: Proot-distro performance issues
source_issues.evidence: Detailed analysis: proot environment introduces syscall overhead, slower filesystem access, and limited process/signal handling. These cause slower startup, tool execution latency, streaming lag, and higher CPU usage. Affects a growing mobile developer audience relying on Termux + proot-distro, which is popular due to YouTube tutorials.

signals.topic: Agent final answer quality degrades when hitting max_steps due to missing FinalAnswerTool usage
signals.summary: When ToolCallingAgent reaches max_steps and calls provide_final_answer, it bypasses FinalAnswerTool, resulting in verbose final answers containing model explanations instead of clean direct answers. This is a confirmed bug in v1.9.2 with concrete code location evidence.
aliases: verbose final answer on agent timeout
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed bug with real user impact: when the agent reaches max_steps, the final answer quality degrades because provide_final_answer bypasses FinalAnswerTool, producing verbose explanatory text instead of a clean direct answer. Code location is explicitly pointed to (agents.py:1425-1427), version v1.9.2 is specified, and the bug has a clear behavioral impact on the main output of the agent. Although count=1 prevents a P0 rating, the evidence of actual workflow degradation warrants P2 retention.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Use FinalAnswerTool to submit final answer after reaching max steps.
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with confirmed reproduction in v1.9.2. Code reference at agents.py line 1425-1427 shows provide_final_answer does not invoke FinalAnswerTool, causing final answers to contain verbose model explanations instead of clean answers.

signals.topic: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware reject decision causes infinite interrupt loop — LLM retries rejected tool indefinitely

aliases: tool rejection causes infinite interrupt loop
signals.review_reason: reject 决策触发无限 interrupt 循环，用户审批功能完全失效。虽 count=2（非高频），但影响的是 HumanInTheLoopMiddleware 这一关键安全/审批功能，且文档明确承诺不会重试，实际行为与文档矛盾，属于主流程阻断（P1）。

source_issues.title: HumanInTheLoopMiddleware: reject decision causes infinite interrupt loop — LLM retries rejected tool indefinitely
source_issues.evidence: reject 决策后 LLM 收到 status="error"，将其理解为临时失败并重试相同工具，触发新 interrupt → 无限循环。用户无法正常使用人工审批功能。根因已定位：_process_decision 返回 tool_call 而非 None，导致 rejected tool_call 保留在 revised_tool_calls 中

signals.topic: CompositeBackend accepts invalid route prefixes silently causing data loss with no exception or log
signals.summary: CompositeBackend 的构造函数对路由前缀不进行验证（文档要求必须以 / 开头且以 / 结尾，但未强制），当用户配置错误前缀（如 "schemas" 缺少前导斜杠）时，路由匹配永远失败，所有写入静默落入 default backend，无日志、无异常、调用方无法区分是正确行为还是数据丢失。
signals.review_reason: 静默数据丢失是严重用户体验问题：配置错误时零反馈、零日志，用户以为写入成功但实际写入错误位置，后续工具依赖错误路径时会级联失败。这比显式报错危险得多，符合 P1 标准。

source_issues.title: feat(backend): validate CompositeBackend route prefixes at construction time
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供明确根因：路由前缀 "schemas"（缺少 /）编译通过但运行时匹配失败，所有写入静默路由到 default backend，无日志无异常无报错。代码位置已定位（libs/deepagents/deepagents/backends/composite.py:141-166），参照 FilesystemPermission.__post_init__ 的现有验证模式可修复。

signals.topic: CompositeBackend route isolation leaks across shared storage backends — routes not properly isolated
signals.summary: CompositeBackend 的路由隔离机制存在缺陷，在共享存储后端场景下，原本应被路由隔离的路径可以被跨路由访问，导致数据隔离失效。这对于多租户或需要权限隔离的场景是严重安全/正确性问题。
signals.review_reason: 数据隔离泄漏直接影响系统正确性，多租户或权限敏感场景下会导致数据混淆。比崩溃更难察觉（静默发生），且可能造成不可逆数据损害，符合 P1 标准。

source_issues.title: CompositeBackend route isolation leaks across shared storage backends

signals.topic: OpenAI Responses API streaming produces duplicate tool_calls in AIMessage content_blocks (partial fc_ prefixed + final call_ prefixed), causing API rejection on serialization/deserialization
signals.summary: When using ChatOpenAI(use_responses_api=True, streaming=True), AIMessage.content_blocks includes both partial 'fc_' prefixed tool_call blocks (empty args, from streaming) and final 'call_' prefixed blocks (full args). content_blocks deduplication by ID only means both survive. On serialization via content_blocks and deserialization, the fc_ blocks with empty args remain, causing OpenAI API to reject with 'No tool output found for function call fc_xxx' on the next turn.
aliases: OpenAI Responses API streaming tool_calls duplication
signals.review_reason: count=2 (one open, one closed duplicate). Reproducible on every use of ChatOpenAI with Responses API + streaming. Causes API-level rejection (BadRequestError) on the next agent turn after any tool call, completely breaking the agent workflow. This is a primary flow failure.

source_issues.title: Duplicate tool_calls in content_blocks with OpenAI Responses API streaming
source_issues.evidence: Minimal repro shows after serialization-deserialization, tool_calls includes fc_ prefixed entries with empty args. API rejects: 'No tool output found for function call fc_12345'. Root cause: deduplication by ID only, fc_xxx != call_xxx.

source_issues.title: Duplicate tool_calls in content_blocks with OpenAI Responses API streaming

signals.topic: merge_dicts concatenates ls_provider string across streaming chunks, inflating AIMessage response_metadata and causing request payload bloat
signals.summary: merge_dicts() in langchain-core concatenates string values when merging streaming chunks. The skip-concatenation guard protects model_provider but omits ls_provider. After ~20 streaming chunks, ls_provider becomes 'amazon_bedrockamazon_bedrock...' (280 chars instead of 14). Every AIMessage in conversation history carries inflated metadata, contributing to request payload bloat in production LangGraph agents with 58+ graph steps.
signals.review_reason: Non-blocking but real user impact: inflated metadata causes request payload bloat in production agents with many steps. The corruption is reproducible on every streaming response. Observability metrics (LangSmith dashboards, cost tracking) are affected when ls_provider is garbage text.

source_issues.title: Bug: merge_dicts concatenates ls_provider across streaming chunks, inflating response_metadata
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows ls_provider grows to 280 chars after 20 chunks instead of 14. Production LangGraph agent with 58+ graph steps observes massively inflated ls_provider across all AIMessages. Proposed fix adds 'ls_provider' to the existing skip-concatenation guard.

signals.topic: ChatAnthropic usage_metadata.input_token_details.cache_creation reports 0 instead of actual token count when tokens are written to cache
signals.summary: When Anthropic prompt caching writes tokens to cache, usage_metadata['input_token_details']['cache_creation'] incorrectly reports 0, while response_metadata['usage']['cache_creation_input_tokens'] correctly shows 12030. The cache_read field in the same dict is accurate. Callers relying on the normalized usage_metadata surface see no cache activity even when 12k+ tokens were cached, breaking cost dashboards, tests, and observability tooling.
signals.review_reason: Non-blocking but definite user impact: cache token metrics (critical for cost estimation) are wrong on every Anthropic API call that writes to cache. Cost dashboards, observability tests, and billing reconciliation all rely on the normalized usage_metadata surface. Related to #32818 which partially fixed this class of bug but left the cache_creation derivation broken.

source_issues.title: ChatAnthropic: usage_metadata.input_token_details.cache_creation is 0 when tokens were written to cache

signals.topic: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently drops values after Overwrite in concurrent supersteps
signals.summary: Silent data loss in concurrent state updates when Overwrite precedes regular values in channel update batches — no error is raised, data is silently discarded.
aliases: channel update drops values after Overwrite
silent data corruption in concurrent writes
signals.review_reason: Silent data loss — no error is raised when values are dropped, making this especially dangerous. In concurrent supersteps, task write ordering is determined by path sorting, not user intent, so any user with parallel tasks writing to the same channel can silently lose data without knowing. Count=2 confirms this is a confirmed, recurring issue.

source_issues.title: bug: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently drops values arriving after Overwrite
source_issues.evidence: In concurrent supersteps, task write ordering is determined by path sorting, not user intent. If Task A writes Overwrite(base) and Task B writes a regular value, and A sorts first, Task B's value is silently lost. ch.update([Overwrite(10), 5]) results in 10 instead of expected 15, with no error raised.

source_issues.title: BinaryOperatorAggregate silently drops regular values that appear after an Overwrite
source_issues.evidence: channel.update([5, Overwrite(10), 3]) silently drops the '3', final value is 10 instead of raising InvalidUpdateError. The update() method completely discards values with no warning when Overwrite precedes them in the same batch.

signals.topic: Second regenerate from same checkpoint silently overwrites branch instead of creating new one (regression in 1.1.7)
signals.summary: Regression in 1.1.7 where consecutive regenerate/time-travel from the same checkpoint overwrites branches instead of creating siblings, causing silent data loss.
aliases: time travel overwrites instead of forking
signals.review_reason: Regression that causes silent data loss during time travel/regeneration — a core multi-branch workflow feature. When a user regenerates from the same checkpoint twice, branches are silently overwritten instead of being created. This directly breaks the multi-branch conversation model and cannot be worked around by users.

source_issues.title: Regression in 1.1.7 (#7498): Second regenerate from latest checkpoint doesn't create new branch
source_issues.evidence: Since 1.1.7, calling astream twice with the same parent checkpoint_id (regenerate) fails to create a second sibling branch. On the 2nd consecutive time-travel, 'latest' is already a fork checkpoint from the previous regenerate — logic either skips or overwrites instead of creating a new sibling. AI output silently overwrites branch 2 instead of creating branch 3.

signals.topic: SyncPregelLoop caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes, bypassing retry logic with CachePolicy
signals.summary: Using CachePolicy with the sync API causes failed or interrupted task errors to be cached and replayed as valid results on re-invocation, completely bypassing retry.
aliases: error writes cached on sync path
signals.review_reason: CachePolicy with sync API silently masks task failures by replaying error writes as valid results, completely bypassing retry logic. Users believe operations succeeded when they actually failed — this is a critical data integrity failure with no user-visible indication of the problem.

source_issues.title: bug: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes caches INTERRUPT/ERROR writes (async path already guarded)
source_issues.evidence: SyncPregelLoop.put_writes persists task writes to cache unconditionally. With CachePolicy enabled, a task that fails or is interrupted has its error writes cached. On re-invocation with same inputs, the cache replays those writes as a valid result, bypassing retry logic entirely. Async path already has a guard that prevents this — sync path is missing it.

signals.topic: Parallel interrupt() calls generate identical IDs, making multi-interrupt resume impossible
signals.summary: Multiple parallel tools each calling interrupt() all receive the same ID, causing resume dict key collision where only one tool can be resumed.
signals.review_reason: Users who execute multiple parallel tools that each call interrupt() cannot resume all of them — all interrupts share the same ID due to namespace key collision, making multi-interrupt workflows impossible. Only one tool can receive a resume value while others are permanently stuck.

source_issues.title: `interrupt()` calls in parallel tools generate identical IDs, making multi-interrupt resume impossible
source_issues.evidence: Multiple tools executing in parallel within the same ToolNode all call interrupt() and receive the SAME ID. The interrupt ID is generated by hashing only the checkpoint namespace, which is shared by all parallel tools in the same node. When building the resume dict, all entries collapse into 1 due to key collision. Only one tool can be resumed; others are permanently stuck.

signals.topic: collections.abc generic containers cause TypeError crash when used in state schema

plugin daemon unable to locate model schemas on cloud

empty array treated as null in HTTP node

signals.topic: Plugin auto-upgrade silently fails — worker reports success but plugin daemon cannot find package

The scheduled worker dispatches upgrade tasks, logs show HTTP 200 success from the plugin daemon, but the daemon fails because the package file does not exist in its local storage. The failure is completely silent from the worker side — only daemon logs reveal the error. The plugin stays on the old version. Root cause: the auto-upgrade task path is missing the download-from-marketplace and upload-to-daemon steps that the manual upgrade path correctly performs.
aliases: plugin upgrade reports success but doesn't install

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor 沙箱缺失导致任意代码执行风险

signals.review_reason: Issue #7462 明确记录了 LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor 将 LLM 生成代码直接写入磁盘并以无沙箱子进程执行的实现路径，具体指出了代码行号(391-434)。提供了具体攻击场景：提示注入触发恶意 subprocess 调用读取 SSH 私钥并外传。影响覆盖：系统完整沦陷、凭证窃取、内网横移，具备明确的用户可感知危害。唯一防护仅一个可被生产环境静默过滤的 UserWarning。该问题在快速启动文档中被直接推荐使用，生产用户极有可能在无感知情况下部署到生产环境，造成真实危害。满足痛点定义中的关键功能安全缺失+明显成本损失风险，符合保留标准。

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing

signals.topic: MCP stdio client browser lock collisions block agent automation mid-session

signals.review_reason: Agent automation (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) is a key use case for Playwright MCP. Mid-session blocking for 10 minutes is a significant workflow disruption. The issue provides exact root cause location and a targeted fix. Two prior related issues (#1214, #1311 in playwright-mcp) indicate this is a known, recurring problem.

source_issues.title: fix(mcp): stdio default profile lock collisions for agent clients

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names is enabled

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: VertexAIGeminiChatCompletion 400 bad request when model makes multiple function calls in one message

signals.topic: Async Responses .parse() causes unbounded memory leak — Pydantic SchemaValidator/Serializer allocated on every call

Pydantic's model_rebuild returns False for unresolved TypeVars, so a new SchemaValidator/SchemaSerializer (heavy Rust objects) is allocated on every call with no upper bound. In long-running servers this causes linear RSS growth and eventual OOM crash.

signals.topic: Persistent ACP session client not returned to pool — forces cold-start on every send (Linux)

signals.topic: Ajv compile() memory leak in long-running gateway process causes OOM and process crash requiring manual restart
signals.summary: sharedAjv.compile() is called per invocation across 6 hot call sites without memoization or cleanup, causing linear memory growth of SchemaEnv/run closures. Over ~3.5h at ~1 compile/sec, heap grows +114 MiB and RSS grows from ~710 MB to ~1.84 GB, eventually triggering V8 OOM and killing the process. Systemd restart is required to recover, blocking the gateway from serving traffic.
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed user pain point with direct production impact: the Ajv schema compilation is called without memoization at 6 distinct hot call sites (ask, llm_invoke, pipeline resume, SDK validate, and two workflow steps), causing linear memory growth that exhausts V8 heap in ~3.5 hours of normal usage. The process crashes with OOM and requires manual systemd restart, which is a main-flow blockage for a long-running gateway service. Three separate OOM incidents were documented in production (Apr 16, 19, 23). Heap profiling with CDP snapshots confirmed the leak is in Ajv's internal compile path (SchemaEnv, closure:run, ValueScopeName, _Code, Name all grow 1:1 with compile calls). This is not a theoretical leak — it is a recurring production incident that blocks user workflows and requires active monitoring/workaround (nightly restart cron). The severity qualifies as a user pain point under '主流程失败/阻断' (main flow failure/blockage) and '明显成本损失' (operational cost of repeated restarts).

source_issues.title: Memory leak: Ajv .compile() per call in sharedAjv leaks SchemaEnv/run closures

Heap profiling confirmed linear growth: +9,693 SchemaEnv, +9,809 closure:run objects accumulated over 3h35m at ~1 compile/sec. V8 --max-old-space-size=2048 exhausted, triggering JavaScript heap out of memory. Requires systemd restart to recover. Affects all 6 call sites: ask.ts, llm_invoke.ts, pipeline_resume_state.ts, SDK validate, and two workflow/file.ts sites.

signals.topic: Authentication failure retry loop triggers gateway rate limiter, blocking device connection

This floods the gateway with auth attempts, triggers its rate limiter, and fills logs with hundreds of identical errors per minute, making the rate limit condition worse.
aliases: gateway rate limiter triggered by auth failures
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed bug with explicit user impact evidence: auth failures cause a tight retry loop that floods the gateway, triggers its rate limiter, and worsens the rate limit condition (each retry resets cooldown). The device is effectively blocked from connecting to the gateway. Log evidence shows hundreds of identical errors per minute. This blocks the core 'device connects to gateway' main flow. Although count=1 < 3, the severity of auth-blocking with rate-limit amplification warrants P1.

source_issues.title: bug: aggressive retry loop on authentication failures triggers gateway rate limiter
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed bug: auth failures (token mismatch, origin rejected, device signature invalid) retry every ~1s with counter reset, never triggering backoff. signals.topic: IngestionPipeline multi-worker mode silently discards all cache writes, causing repeated expensive re-embeddings
signals.summary: When IngestionPipeline runs with num_workers > 1, worker processes mutate their own in-memory cache copies that are lost on worker exit. No cache state is merged back. Subsequent runs re-execute all transformations (including embedding) as if uncached, silently wasting compute proportional to corpus size. Pipeline.persist() also omits worker-created entries.
aliases: pipeline cache not merged after parallel ingestion
signals.review_reason: P0 because it causes direct monetary cost (repeated embedding on unchanged documents scales linearly with corpus size and re-indexing frequency) and is completely silent — users are unaware they are paying for redundant compute. The root cause is deterministic and reproducible with the multi-worker path.

signals.topic: RedisVectorStore.add/async_add returns corrupted node IDs due to misuse of .strip() instead of .removeprefix()
signals.summary: RedisVectorStore uses Python's .strip(chars) to remove the Redis key prefix from node IDs. Since .strip() removes individual characters not the exact substring, UUIDs whose hex characters overlap with the prefix prefix characters get truncated. This silently corrupts node IDs returned to the caller, breaking any downstream logic that depends on original node IDs (caching, deletion, retrieval lookups).
aliases: strip() corrupts UUID node IDs in Redis store
signals.review_reason: P1: data corruption in a core vector store operation. The returned IDs no longer match the original node IDs, breaking cache lookups, deletion, and citation tracking. The bug is silent (no exception), so users may not notice data corruption until search/deletion fails. Only affects node IDs whose UUIDs start with characters present in the Redis prefix.

signals.topic: QueryFusionRetriever silently ignores retriever_weights when mode='reciprocal_rerank', producing incorrect fused results

signals.review_reason: P1: silent incorrect results in a core retrieval fusion feature. When users explicitly configure retriever weights (a documented parameter), the weights are silently ignored with no error or warning. This breaks multi-retriever RAG pipelines where weighting signals matters.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: QueryFusionRetriever ignores retriever_weights when mode='reciprocal_rerank'

signals.review_reason: P1: breaks a core user expectation — that a retriever's response contains source_nodes for citation. This is a fundamental RAG contract. The failure is silent and breaks applications using response.source_nodes for attribution, groundedness checking, or UX citation display.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: TreeSelectLeafRetriever query path returns empty source_nodes

signals.topic: Node.hash uses MetadataMode.ALL including volatile file-stat metadata, triggering unnecessary full re-embeddings on every ingestion run
signals.summary: Since PR #18303, Node.hash includes all metadata via MetadataMode.ALL, ignoring excluded_embed_metadata_keys. SimpleDirectoryReader populates file-stat fields (last_modified_date, creation_date, last_accessed_date, file_size) which change on every filesystem read. A hash mismatch triggers vector_store.delete() + full re-embed on the next IngestionPipeline.run(), even for byte-identical documents. Silent and scales with corpus size, modification rate, and re-indexing frequency.
aliases: Node.hash includes file atime causing spurious re-embeddings
signals.review_reason: P1: causes significant wasted compute in a common pipeline (SimpleDirectoryReader + IngestionPipeline) used in production RAG systems. The trigger is silent and deterministic. Users pay for repeated full re-embeddings of unchanged documents. The cost is proportional to corpus size and re-indexing frequency.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Node.hash uses MetadataMode.ALL, causing unnecessary re-embeds when volatile file-stat metadata changes
source_issues.evidence: Linux relatime updates atime on read. Container environments, NFS, SMB mounts commonly update stat metadata. The pipeline silently re-embeds unchanged content — no warning, no log. Cost scales with corpus size, modification rate, and re-indexing frequency.

signals.topic: Node.js runtime emits DEP0169 url.parse() deprecation warning on every cold start, polluting production error logs
